stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Hemanth is immediately above Kavya.
2. Isha is exactly 3 positions above Zoya.
3. In the stated ordering, Isha comes before Yuvraj, and Yuvraj comes before Hemanth.
4. Charu is at floor 3.
stimuli.solution: floor 1: Zoya; floor 2: Dev; floor 3: Charu; floor 4: Isha; floor 5: Yuvraj; floor 6: Kavya; floor 7: Hemanth

stimuli.title: Seven labelled boxes are stacked vertically, with one box in each position.

stimuli.title: Seven people have interviews in seven consecutive months from January to July, one per month.
stimuli.body:

1. Nisha is exactly 2 positions later than Jai.
2. Farhan is at May.
3. There are exactly 1 positions between Bharat and Farhan.

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
almond winter thunder = zu no di
forest bridge winter = ka di mu
bridge honest almond = ka ju zu
thunder forest honest = ju no mu
stimuli.solution: winter=di, almond=zu, thunder=no, bridge=ka, forest=mu, honest=ju

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X > V < S ≥ W < T, decide which conclusions follow. I: W < T. II: V ≤ S.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W ≥ T ≥ U ≥ R < P, decide which conclusions follow. I: W ≥ T. II: W ≥ R.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain V < W < U > R > Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: V = R. II: U ≥ Z.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z > X < S < Q ≥ V, decide which conclusions follow. I: S ≥ Q. II: Q < V.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z = R < U < T < V, decide which conclusions follow. I: T > V. II: U < T.

questions.stem: Statements: Some dancers are painters. Some painters are drivers. Conclusions: I. Some dancers are drivers. II. Some painters are dancers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The two Some overlaps need not coincide; Some A are B converts to Some B are A.

questions.stem: Statements: All pilots are drivers. Some farmers are pilots. Conclusions: I. Some farmers are drivers. II. Some drivers are farmers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No poets are sailors. All bakers are sailors. Some bakers are sailors. Conclusions: I. No poets are bakers. II. Some bakers are not poets. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some coders are readers. Some readers are sailors. Conclusions: I. Some coders are sailors. II. All sailors are coders. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some painters are runners. All runners are workers. Conclusions: I. Some painters are workers. II. All painters are workers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 105 km north, then 84 km east, then 21 km south and finally 21 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net north = 84 km and east = 63 km. Distance = √(84²+63²) = 105 km.

questions.stem: Kiran moves 21 km north, 126 km east, 63 km south and 21 km west. In which direction is Kiran from the start?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 189 km north, 84 km east, 105 km south and 21 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
questions.explanation: Total path length = 189+84+105+21=399 km (not displacement).
